{{Current events|year=2019|month=10|day=24|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->

;International relations
*[[Japan–South Korea relations]], [[2019 Japan–South Korea trade dispute]]
**Japan and South Korea hold a high-level bilateral meeting for the first time since the trade dispute, with Japanese Prime Minister [[Shinzō Abe]] meeting with his counterpart [[Lee Nak-yeon]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/10/24/national/politics-diplomacy/abe-meets-south-korean-prime-minister/#.XbFdXnPZHqA (''The Japan Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Grays incident]]
**The people found deceased in a lorry in [[Essex]] yesterday are suspected to be Chinese nationals. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-essex-50162617 (BBC News)] 
*[[Uganda Anti-Homosexuality Act, 2014|Persecution of homosexuals in Uganda]]
**Ugandan authorities announce that they have arrested 16 [[LGBT activist]]s on suspicion of [[gay sex]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/24/sixteen-lgbt-activists-arrested-in-uganda-as-hate-crimes-soar (''The Guardian'')]
*At the [[Old Bailey]] a [[United Kingdom|UK]] jury convicts a British man who traveled to fight against the [[Islamic State]] of a terror offence for visiting a training camp used by the [[PKK]]. He is the first UK man found guilty of such a crime, and is remanded in custody to await his November 7 sentencing hearing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-50167158 (BBC News)]
;Politics and elections
*The remains of former Spanish dictator [[Francisco Franco]] are exhumed from [[Valle de los Caídos]] and are moved to a private mausoleum with his wife [[Carmen Polo]], 44 years after his death. Some pro-Franco protestors gather outside the national mausoleum. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/24/europe/franco-exhumation-spain-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2019 Lebanese protests]]
**As protests enter its eighth day, [[President of Lebanon|President]] [[Michel Aoun]] in a televised address states he is willing to meet with protestors and offers support for various reforms, such as increasing transparency for banks and lifting [[Absolute immunity|immunity for government officials]]. He however states that changes “can only happen through state institutions" in response to calls to bring down the government. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/waiting-lebanon-aoun-invites-protesters-talk-191024112324367.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Chicago Teachers Union]]'s strike enters its sixth school day as it is unable to reach an agreement with [[Chicago Public Schools]]. [https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/cps-classes-canceled-for-sixth-day-thursday-chicago-teachers-strike-563728431.html (WMAQ-TV)]
*[[Special Counsel investigation (2017-2019)]], [[Russia investigation origins counter-narrative]]
**U.S. federal prosecutor [[John Durham]]'s ongoing probe into potential [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] and [[United States Department of Justice| Justice Department]] misconduct in the time leading up to the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]] through the spring of 2017 is upgraded to a formal criminal investigation. [https://nypost.com/2019/10/24/justice-department-review-of-russia-probe-is-now-a-criminal-probe/?fbclid=IwAR0mmeqqYw9n-1vR6lZJFwmpZ9vEP9CM3ga6Kx4j90uOklSiEu5YY4XIeYU (''New York Post'')]

;Sports
*[[Brandon Taubman]], the assistant general manager for the [[Houston Astros]], is fired from his position for making "inappropriate comments" toward female journalists. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/barrymbloom/2019/10/24/brandon-taubman-fired-by-houston-astros-for-inappropriate-conduct/?fbclid=IwAR3s7kXzh1WPBjA2Hb54LCeTfKrE-cIg4IkeMFCyxhgE8Tq_u-eNeUyLyyI#6d40c3586d80 (''Forbes'')]
